text:
anita: Heads up — since the 2026-03-17 runtime roll (merged by @prashant) we've seen a sustained ~30% drop in tokens/sec on the ctb serving pool. p50 latency up ~12ms, p95 up ~85ms. KV cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 18%.
kevin: ugh. any obvious rollout note? which change touched scheduling or kernel routing?
deploy-bot: deploy: runtime-service v3.8.1 rolled to ctb-prod at 2026-03-17T02:14Z (sha: a3b9f4c). Canary passed.
hiro: I ran a quick perf trace. Scheduler is emitting lots of 1-2 request batches during steady qps. Batcher drain rate looks noisy (saw repeated wakeups instead of coalesced window). Also saw kernel fallback in logs: "kernel=generic_mm" for several long requests.
sara: can you paste the flame/trace?
hiro: pastebin: https://s3.redwood-inference/profiles/1973456789/ctb-flame.svg (private link). Short snippet of the hot path: ```
Scheduler::try_emit_batch() {
  if (prefetch_hint) schedule_immediate(); // new heuristic in this diff
  ..collect.. if (collected_count <= 2) emit_small_batch();
}
```
anita: those two lines are from the new prefetch heuristic PR that tried to lower latency for short seqs. Looks like it is preempting batching and thrashing the coalescer. KV cache misses likely because prefetches race with cache population.
kevin: ok quick mitigation: flip the feature flag off in prod for ctb and observe. Flag: `runtime.ctb.prefetch_immediate=false`
hiro: ran the flag flip on one zone — tokens/sec recovered ~22% within 90s, p95 back to ~baseline, KV miss rate trending down. Not fully recovered though.
sara: sounds like a rollout blocker. we should bisect which commit introduced the prefetch change vs kernel-routing side effects. Prashant's merge included both prefetch and a kernel selection tweak, right?
maria: yes — PR #4287 had two unrelated commits. If we hold the rollout until a proper split + test we should be safe. Recommend canary-hold and revert the prefetch subcommit.
eng-oncall-bot: alert: ctb-pool-tokenrate-drop firing -> paging eng-runtime oncall.
kevin: I'll open a revert PR that strips the prefetch_immediate path and add a unit+perf test for batching entropy (simulate steady qps of mixed seq lengths). Assigning to @kevin/@hiro.
anita: also add a perf regression CI job that runs a small CTB harness with KV warmup to catch cache thrash. Current CI doesn't exercise KV warm paths.
maria: filing follow-up: https://issues.redwood/INF-1023 — split PR, add canary gating, CI perf job.
hiro: for the bisect notes — suspect range a3b9f4c (merge) -> a3b9f4c^1 where prefetch_delta exists. I'll run `git bisect run` with the microbench harness and report back. Command I used: ```
GOPROFILE=cpu.out ./tools/ctb_perf_test --qps=200 --mix=short:60,long:40 --warm_kv=true
```
kevin: thanks. keep thread updated. small rollback + new test should unblock the rollout quickly. :thumbsup:
